name: Mountain
overview: Scripture reveals mountains as significant places of divine encounter and revelation. For example, Abraham was instructed to offer Isaac on a mountain in Moriah, later known as Mount Zion, the site of the temple (Genesis 22:2). Mount Horeb was appointed as a place for Israel to worship God, marked by a powerful manifestation of His presence with fire, darkness, and cloud (Exodus 3:12; Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:23). Mountains also symbolize God's judgment against idolatry, as Israel was commanded to destroy high places where false gods were worshiped (Deuteronomy 12:2), and they can represent awe-inspiring displays of God's power, such as when the mountains melted before the LORD at Sinai (Judges 5:5).
